{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "# Fizzy

Guidance for AI coding agents working with this repository.

Fizzy is a kanban-style project management and issue tracker: cards move across columns on boards, with comments, mentions, and assignments.

## Deploy

Default branch: `main`

Self-hosted deploys run Kamal against `config/deploy.yml` — see `docs/kamal-deployment.md`.

## SaaS mode

For local agent work, `tmp/saas.txt` is the checkout-level SaaS switch used by `bin/setup`. When present, read `saas/AGENTS.md` before continuing. Otherwise, do not apply its instructions.

## Architecture Overview

### Multi-Tenancy (URL-Based)

Fizzy uses **URL path-based multi-tenancy**:
- Accounts have a unique decimal `external_account_id` used in URL prefixes
- URLs are prefixed: `/{account_id}/boards/...`
- Middleware (`AccountSlug::Extractor`) extracts the account ID from the URL and sets `Current.account`
- The slug is moved from `PATH_INFO` to `SCRIPT_NAME`, making Rails think it's "mounted" at that path
- Tenant-scoped domain records are account-isolated; global identity, session, and authentication records are exceptions
- Background jobs automatically serialize and restore account context

**Key insight**: This architecture allows multi-tenancy without subdomains or separate databases, making local development and testing simpler.

### Authentication & Authorization

Passwordless magic link authentication. A global `Identity` (email-based) can have `Users` in multiple Accounts, so an email is not a single account membership. Users have roles: owner, admin, member, system. Board-level access control via `Access` records.

### Entropy System

Cards automatically "postpone" (move to "not now") after inactivity:
- Account-level default entropy period
- Board-level entropy override
- Prevents endless todo lists from accumulating
- Configurable via Account/Board settings

### UUID Primary Keys

All tables use UUIDs (UUIDv7 format, base36-encoded as 25-char strings):
- Custom fixture UUID generation maintains deterministic ordering for tests
- Fixtures are always "older" than runtime records
- `.first`/`.last` work correctly in tests

### Background Jobs (Solid Queue)

Database-backed job queue (no Redis):
- Custom `FizzyActiveJobExtensions` prepended to ActiveJob
- Jobs automatically capture/restore `Current.account`
- Mission Control::Jobs for monitoring

Recurring tasks are declared in `config/recurring.yml`.

### Sharded Full-Text Search

Full-text search runs in the database, not Elasticsearch. On MySQL it is sharded 16 ways by CRC32 of the account ID (`Search::Record::Trilogy`); on SQLite it is a single FTS5 index (`Search::Record::SQLite`). Don't assume the sharded shape when working under SQLite. Models in `app/models/search/`.

### Imports and exports

Allow people to move between OSS and SAAS Fizzy instances:
- Exports/Imports can be written to/read from local or S3 storage depending on the config of the instance (both must be supported)
- Must be able to handle very large ZIP files (500+GB)
- Models in `app/models/account/data_transfer/`, `app/models/zip_file`

## Coding style

Before editing or reviewing code, read STYLE.md.
=== STYLE.md ===

# Style

We aim to write code that is a pleasure to read, and we have a lot of opinions about how to do it well. Writing great code is an essential part of our programming culture, and we deliberately set a high bar for every code change anyone contributes. We care about how code reads, how code looks, and how code makes you feel when you read it.

We love discussing code. If you have questions about how to write something, or if you detect some smell you are not quite sure how to solve, please ask away to other programmers. A Pull Request is a great way to do this.

When writing new code, unless you are very familiar with our approach, try to find similar code elsewhere to look for inspiration.

## Conditional returns

In general, we prefer to use expanded conditionals over guard clauses.

```ruby
# Bad
def todos_for_new_group
  ids = params.require(:todolist)[:todo_ids]
  return [] unless ids
  @bucket.recordings.todos.find(ids.split(","))
end

# Good
def todos_for_new_group
  if ids = params.require(:todolist)[:todo_ids]
    @bucket.recordings.todos.find(ids.split(","))
  else
    []
  end
end
```

This is because guard clauses can be hard to read, especially when they are nested.

As an exception, we sometimes use guard clauses to return early from a method:

* When the return is right at the beginning of the method.
* When the main method body is not trivial and involves several lines of code.

```ruby
def after_recorded_as_commit(recording)
  return if recording.parent.was_created?

  if recording.was_created?
    broadcast_new_column(recording)
  else
    broadcast_column_change(recording)
  end
end
```

## Methods ordering

We order methods in classes in the following order:

1. `class` methods
2. `public` methods with `initialize` at the top.
3. `private` methods

## Invocation order

We order methods vertically based on their invocation order. This helps us to understand the flow of the code.

```ruby
class SomeClass
  def some_method
    method_1
    method_2
  end

  private
    def method_1
      method_1_1
      method_1_2
    end
  
    def method_1_1
      # ...
    end
  
    def method_1_2
      # ...
    end
  
    def method_2
      method_2_1
      method_2_2
    end
  
    def method_2_1
      # ...
    end
  
    def method_2_2
      # ...
    end
end
```

## To bang or not to bang

Should I call a method `do_something` or `do_something!`?

As a general rule, we only use `!` for methods that have a correspondent counterpart without `!`. In particular, we don’t use `!` to flag destructive actions. There are plenty of destructive methods in Ruby and Rails that do not end with `!`.

## Visibility modifiers

We don't add a newline under visibility modifiers, and we indent the content under them.

```ruby
class SomeClass
  def some_method
    # ...
  end

  private
    def some_private_method_1
      # ...
    end

    def some_private_method_2
      # ...
    end
end
```

If a module only has private methods, we mark it `private` at the top and add an extra new line after but don't indent.

```ruby
module SomeModule
  private
  
  def some_private_method
    # ...
  end
end
```

## CRUD controllers

We model web endpoints as CRUD operations on resources (REST). When an action doesn't map cleanly to a standard CRUD verb, we introduce a new resource rather than adding custom actions.

```ruby
# Bad
resources :cards do
  post :close
  post :reopen
end

# Good
resources :cards do
  resource :closure
end
```

## Controller and model interactions

In general, we favor a [vanilla Rails](https://dev.37signals.com/vanilla-rails-is-plenty/) approach with thin controllers directly invoking a rich domain model. We don't use services or other artifacts to connect the two.

Invoking plain Active Record operations is totally fine:

```ruby
class Cards::CommentsController < ApplicationController
  def create
    @comment = @card.comments.create!(comment_params)
  end
end
```

For more complex behavior, we prefer clear, intention-revealing model APIs that controllers call directly:

```ruby
class Cards::GoldnessesController < ApplicationController
  def create
    @card.gild
  end
end
```

When justified, it is fine to use services or form objects, but don't treat those as special artifacts:

```ruby
Signup.new(email_address: email_address).create_identity
```

## Run async operations in jobs

As a general rule, we write shallow job classes that delegate the logic itself to domain models:

* We typically use the suffix `_later` to flag methods that enqueue a job.
* A common scenario is having a model class that enqueues a job that, when executed, invokes some method in that same class. In this case, we use the suffix `_now` for the regular synchronous method.

```ruby
module Event::Relaying
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    after_create_commit :relay_later
  end

  def relay_later
    Event::RelayJob.perform_later(self)
  end

  def relay_now
    # ...
  end
end

class Event::RelayJob < ApplicationJob
  def perform(event)
    event.relay_now
  end
end
```

class BoardsController < ApplicationController
  wrap_parameters :board, include: %i[ name all_access auto_postpone_period_in_days public_description ]

  include FilterScoped

  before_action :set_board, except: %i[ index new create ]
  before_action :ensure_permission_to_admin_board, only: %i[ update destroy ]

  def index
    set_page_and_extract_portion_from Current.user.boards.ordered_by_recently_accessed.includes(creator: :identity)
    fresh_when etag: @page.records
  end

  def show
    if @filter.used?(ignore_boards: true)
      show_filtered_cards
    else
      show_columns
    end
  end

  def new
    @board = Board.new
  end

  def create
    @board = Board.create! board_params.with_defaults(all_access: true)

    respond_to do |format|
      format.html { redirect_to board_path(@board) }
      format.json { render :show, status: :created, location: board_path(@board, format: :json) }
    end
  end

  def edit
    selected_user_ids = @board.users.ids
    @selected_users, @unselected_users = \
      @board.account.users.active.alphabetically.includes(:identity).partition { |user| selected_user_ids.include? user.id }
  end

  def update
    @board.update! board_params
    @board.accesses.revise granted: grantees, revoked: revokees if grantees_changed?

    respond_to do |format|
      format.html do
        if @board.accessible_to?(Current.user)
          redirect_to edit_board_path(@board), notice: "Saved"
        else
          redirect_to root_path, notice: "Saved (you were removed from the board)"
        end
      end
      format.json do
        if @board.accessible_to?(Current.user)
          render :show
        else
          head :no_content
        end
      end
    end
  end

  def destroy
    @board.destroy

    respond_to do |format|
      format.html { redirect_to root_path }
      format.json { head :no_content }
    end
  end

  private
    def set_board
      @board = Current.user.boards.find params[:id]
    end

    def ensure_permission_to_admin_board
      unless Current.user.can_administer_board?(@board)
        head :forbidden
      end
    end

    def grantees_changed?
      params.key?(:user_ids)
    end

    def show_filtered_cards
      @filter.board_ids = [ @board.id ]
      set_page_and_extract_portion_from @filter.cards
    end

    def show_columns
      cards = @board.cards.awaiting_triage.latest.with_golden_first.preloaded
      set_page_and_extract_portion_from cards
      fresh_when etag: [ @board, @page.records, @user_filtering, Current.account ]
    end

    def board_params
      params.expect(board: [ :name, :all_access, :auto_postpone_period_in_days, :public_description ])
    end

    def grantees
      @board.account.users.active.where id: grantee_ids
    end

    def revokees
      @board.users.where.not id: grantee_ids
    end

    def grantee_ids
      params.fetch :user_ids, []
    end
end

require "application_system_test_case"

class CardRefreshTest < ApplicationSystemTestCase
  include ActionView::RecordIdentifier

  setup do
    sign_in_as(users(:david))
    Current.user = users(:kevin)
    @card = cards(:layout)
  end

  test "a broadcast refresh shows card changes made elsewhere" do
    visit card_url(@card)
    assert_selector "h1", text: @card.title

    update_card_elsewhere

    assert_selector "h1", text: "Retitled elsewhere", wait: 5
    assert_text "Description updated elsewhere"
  end

  test "a broadcast refresh preserves an edit in progress" do
    visit card_url(@card)
    click_on @card.title

    within_edit_frame do
      fill_in_lexxy with: "Draft description in progress"
    end

    update_card_elsewhere

    # The title change's system comment appearing proves the refresh reached the page.
    assert_text "changed the title", wait: 5
    within_edit_frame do
      assert_selector "lexxy-editor", text: "Draft description in progress"
    end
    assert_no_text "Description updated elsewhere"
  end

  test "canceling an edit reveals card changes made elsewhere during the edit" do
    visit card_url(@card)
    click_on @card.title
    within_edit_frame { assert_selector "form" }

    update_card_elsewhere
    assert_text "changed the title", wait: 5

    send_keys :escape

    assert_selector "h1", text: "Retitled elsewhere"
    assert_text "Description updated elsewhere"
  end

  test "a broadcast refresh shows card changes after an edit is canceled" do
    visit card_url(@card)
    click_on @card.title
    within_edit_frame { assert_selector "form" }

    send_keys :escape
    assert_selector "a.card__title-link", text: @card.title

    update_card_elsewhere

    assert_selector "h1", text: "Retitled elsewhere", wait: 5
    assert_text "Description updated elsewhere"
  end

  private
    def update_card_elsewhere
      wait_for_cable_subscriptions
      @card.update!(title: "Retitled elsewhere", description: "Description updated elsewhere")
      perform_enqueued_jobs only: Turbo::Streams::BroadcastStreamJob
    end

    # A broadcast sent before the page's subscriptions are confirmed is lost.
    def wait_for_cable_subscriptions
      assert_selector "turbo-cable-stream-source[connected]", visible: :all
      assert_no_selector "turbo-cable-stream-source:not([connected])", visible: :all
    end

    def within_edit_frame(&block)
      within "##{dom_id(@card, :edit)}", &block
    end
end

require "test_helper"

class Cards::TriagesControllerTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  setup do
    sign_in_as :kevin
  end

  test "create" do
    card = cards(:logo)
    original_column = card.column
    column = columns(:writebook_in_progress)

    assert_changes -> { card.reload.column }, from: original_column, to: column do
      post card_triage_path(card, column_id: column.id)
      assert_redirected_to card
    end
  end

  test "destroy" do
    card = cards(:shipping)

    assert_changes -> { card.reload.column }, to: nil do
      delete card_triage_path(card), as: :turbo_stream
      assert_redirected_to card
    end
  end

  test "create as JSON" do
    card = cards(:logo)
    column = columns(:writebook_in_progress)

    post card_triage_path(card, column_id: column.id), as: :json

    assert_response :no_content
    assert_equal column, card.reload.column
  end

  test "destroy as JSON" do
    card = cards(:shipping)

    assert card.column.present?

    delete card_triage_path(card), as: :json

    assert_response :no_content
    assert_nil card.reload.column
  end
end

**Okay, let's break down this drop-down card scenario meticulously. I need to be sure the user experience is seamless and that our data integrity is bulletproof. Here's my thought process:**

### Column Header Counts and CSS Variables

I immediately see the clever use of CSS variables (`--card-count`) on the column headers, being updated by `css-variable-counter`. That's a great initial approach. The controller `css_variable_counter_controller.js` is essential here for connecting/disconnecting to the DOM to trigger updates. I'm noting the `maxValue: 15` which ensures that the count remains constrained, which keeps pagination in mind.

My first concern is the visible count in the `<span>` element. This *isn't* automatically updated by the CSS variable counter. This means that if you drag a card to a collapsed column and the server hasn't responded, the displayed count will be stale. I have a solution though! I can update this number optimistically in the front-end when the drop happens, so it reflects the expected state immediately. That way, there's no visible shift or delay. If the server fails, it will roll back and the counts will too.

I'm thinking about the situation when a column has more than 15 cards, which impacts the pagination, and the effect it has if one card is moved in or out. The CSS variable counter should automatically handle that, because it's only counting what's *currently* in the DOM. The `css-variable-counter` will take care of updating the numbers less than 15. The solution is in place.

### The Lifecycle of a Card Drop on the Server

This is the critical part. I need to understand the full flow, from the user's action to the final state.

1.  **HTTP Request:** When the user drops a card, a specific HTTP request is sent based on the target column. The existing routes seem well-designed, but it's important to look at all possible card drop targets.
2.  **Server Response:** The server processes the card move. Key pieces here are Rails' `after_save`, `after_touch` callbacks, and `Board::Broadcastable`'s broadcast refreshes. These all feed into the updating of data.
3.  **ActionCable Broadcast:** `turbo_stream_from @board` is the key. This sends a Turbo Stream refresh to all connected clients.
4.  **Turbo Handling:** This broadcast triggers a `morph` operation on the affected frames. `turbo_refreshes_with` and `turbo_frame_tag` in the view are critical to the refresh. We have `frame_controller.js` to manage the morphing or reloading of elements.

### The Different Drop Target Types

We have four potential drop targets: "Not Now," "Maybe?," custom columns, and "Done." Each has a specific Rails controller and action to handle: `Cards::NotNowsController`, `Cards::TriagesController`, and `Cards::ClosuresController`. We need to be able to get these URLs into our views dynamically based on the state of the card.

We need to make it simple for the user. We have to make sure each column knows how to accept dropped cards, or card knows where to post.

*   **Option A**: Create new RESTful drop endpoints or update our existing ones.

This seems in line with the current RESTful design, but the existing URLs are already nicely set up. We're thinking that with all that already exists in place, it's pretty good. We have a solid foundation!

In all cases, we need to think about the URL that needs to be generated. Let's make sure the card's action URLs are easily available in every context, open *or* closed.

Okay, let's break this down. This is crucial; I need to meticulously map the interaction between the HTTP request, Turbo, and ActionCable, step-by-step. Let's trace the full lifecycle of this card drag-and-drop scenario.

**Analyzing the Drag-and-Drop Card Update Process**

Here's the situation: a user drags Card A from, say, a "Maybe?" column and drops it into an "In Progress" column.

1.  **The Drop Moment (Zero Milliseconds):** This is where it gets interesting! Everything *visually* updates instantly in the DOM. Immediately, the `<article>` element representing the card gets repositioned from the source column's list to the destination's list, in the appropriate sorted position. The card's styling immediately reflects its new column (e.g., the color changes, classes like `.card--postponed` are added/removed). The card counts for both source and destination columns are updated *instantly* using the `.cards__expander-count` element and the `--card-count` CSS variable. If the source column becomes empty, a `.blank-slate--drag` element appears (assuming it's always rendered but controlled by CSS `:has(.card)`). If the destination column was empty, the `.blank-slate--drag` element hides. Finally, any lingering visual clues from the drag-and-drop itself (e.g., `.drag-and-drop__dragged-item`, `.drag-and-drop__hover-container`) get cleaned up.

2.  **Immediately After Drop (Asynchronous, Background Process):** After the initial visual updates, an HTTP request is fired off in the background to persist the change on the server. We're using `@rails/request.js`, probably `post` or `destroy` to handle this. It seems to automatically include the CSRF token, which is essential. But wait a second, a key question arises! **Does `@rails/request.js` *also* send the `X-Turbo-Request-Id` header?** That's the critical question! I need to verify how Turbo identifies and handles its requests, and how it meshes with `broadcasts_refreshes` and `Turbo::Refresh`.

    I need to double-check `vendor/javascript/@rails--request.js` to see what headers this method sends. Then, I will need to understand the connection between that and `turbo` to see what this does to the broadcast workflow. This is key to ensuring that the application behaves correctly with the real-time updates through ActionCable.

**My Analysis of Turbo's Turbo-Powered Optimistic Updates**

Okay, so I've been digging deep into how Turbo is handling these drag-and-drop operations, and it's actually pretty brilliant. Here's what I've found, and the implications:

*   **Turbo's Efficiency:** Turbo uses `X-Turbo-Request-Id` to suppress broadcasted refreshes from the originating client. This is key to preventing visual glitches. The server generates a unique ID, adds it to the list of recent requests, then sends the ID in the request headers. The server then captures this to be used to suppress refreshes.

*   **Optimistic Updates are Key:** The application optimistically moves the card in the DOM immediately. This includes updating classes, colors, counts, and visibility based on the *intended* state. This happens *before* the server even acknowledges the change.

*   **No Content is KING:** The server, in most cases, responds with `204 No Content` after successfully saving the changes. This tells the browser *nothing* should be touched in the DOM. Other users receive broadcasts for refreshes, which is expected.

*   **Server-Side Robustness:** Even if the server responds very slowly (500ms), or the server fails, the application is in a consistent state and handles the situation accordingly.

*   **Edge Case Mastery:** It correctly considers scenarios that could trigger visual shifts or inconsistencies.

    *   Handles empty columns gracefully, switching blank slates.
    *   It renders the necessary data attributes to allow hotkeys to work immediately.
    *   Properly updates card colors, states, and counts for all columns.
    *   Handles scenarios where a card has meta-data, bubbles, or is already closed/postponed.
    *   Handles how a column's `turbo-frame` loads for collapsed columns.
    *   Correctly serializes rapid user actions to ensure consistency.

*   **Serializing is KEY** By queuing requests, we can guarantee that rapid changes, even back-to-back drags, are executed in the correct order. The use of a simple promise queue is perfect!

*   **The Power of Morphing:** When we get a `turbo_stream.replace` with `method: :morph`, it is *crucial* that the server-rendered DOM state *exactly* matches the optimistic state. If the DOM states are already the same, it means *nothing* shifts. This also allows the server to update things like "just now" timestamps and any other subtle updates that were missed in the optimistic update.

*   **Perfect DOM Structure:** The way `.cards__list` is structured with `display-contents` and `turbo-frame[role="presentation"]` makes this possible, because they correctly define the scope and lifecycle of the morphing.

*   **Fault Tolerance:** In the (rare) event the server request fails, the application keeps track of the original state, and can roll back to it if the request doesn't succeed.

This is a well-thought-out system. The use of optimistic updates combined with the No Content response is a clever and efficient way to provide a smooth user experience. The serialization of the request queue prevents errors and ensures data integrity.

steps.reasoning_content:
**Deep Dive into Card Drag and Drop Implementation**

Okay, so I've been diving deep into this drag-and-drop feature, and I've uncovered some pretty slick stuff. It's all about how these cards move around and how they appear when they're being dragged.  First, this `display: contents` thing is *amazing*. It lets the cards flow as if they were flex children directly under the column, no matter where they are in the DOM.  This is super important for our layout.

Now, the insertion algorithm is key. We have four types of columns, each with its own ordering: Maybe, Custom Columns (golden cards first, then last active), Not Now (just last active), and Done (recently closed).  The *magic* is that moving a card always sets `last_active_at` to `Time.current`. That means in non-golden-first columns, the dragged card *always* goes at the top. In golden-first, the logic checks if the card being moved is golden and places it accordingly relative to other golden cards. The logic is clean and precise. It handles empty columns, columns with only golden cards, and the different pagination cases, all flawlessly.

Next, I needed to figure out how to *actually* implement the drag. We're using HTML5 Drag and Drop, not Pointer Events. I figured this out because of how we’re using `draggable: false` on links within the card (`.card__link`), and `draggable="true"` on the whole card element.  And, because of the CSS that dims the original card and doesn’t use any floating drag ghost styling. HTML5 Drag and Drop is definitely the way to go.

Here's the detailed breakdown of the logic:

*   **Gotcha 1:** Clicking vs. dragging. By setting `draggable=false` on the link and `draggable=true` on the card, clicking works as expected and dragging drags the card. Any child elements are covered by the link, so dragging works on the card as well.
*   **Gotcha 2:** The drag image. Adding the dimmed style synchronously in `dragstart` results in the dimmed image being captured. Adding it on an animation frame ensures the full-color card appears first.
*   **Gotcha 3:** Firefox needs `setData`. Also setting `effectAllowed` and `dropEffect` is good practice.
*   **Gotcha 4:** `dragover` and `preventDefault`.  We need to prevent the default behavior on `dragover` to allow dropping. We're also doing nothing when the drag source and destination are the same column, so the card just stays where it is.
*   **Gotcha 5:** The flickering issue. Using a tracked `#hoveredContainer` and using `dragenter`/`dragleave` and their `relatedTarget` correctly handles the hover state and prevents flickering when dragging over child elements.
*   **Gotcha 6:** Small viewports and mobile, no drag and drop. We use a Stimulus controller to dynamically enable `draggable="true"` on cards depending on the screen width (desktop) or `draggable="false"` or no `draggable` (mobile and small viewports).
    Stimulus’ `itemTargetConnected` is great, because it automatically enables drag and drop when cards appear via Turbo Frames, pagination or Turbo Streams. This also means we're checking for non-public boards, because those are read-only. We are also able to check if we're on a mobile device and disable drag-and-drop in some cases.

    # queries with a single constant cutoff, so `account_id = ? AND
    # last_active_at <= ?` rides the existing index instead of computing the
    # threshold per row across every card in the system.
    def auto_postpone_all_due(as_of: Time.now)
      Account.find_each do |account|
        account.boards.includes(:entropy).group_by(&:auto_postpone_period).each do |period, boards|
          account.cards.active
            .where(board_id: boards.map(&:id))
            .where(last_active_at: ..(as_of - period))
            .find_each do |card|
              card.auto_postpone(user: account.system_user)
            end
        end
      end
    end
  end

  def entropy
    Card::Entropy.for(self)
  end

  def entropic?
    entropy.present?
  end

require "application_system_test_case"

class BoardDragAndDropTest < ApplicationSystemTestCase
  include ActionView::RecordIdentifier

  setup do
    sign_in_as(users(:david))
    @board = boards(:writebook)
    @triage = columns(:writebook_triage)
    @in_progress = columns(:writebook_in_progress)
    @on_hold = columns(:writebook_on_hold)
  end

  test "dragging a card from Maybe to a collapsed column updates immediately and persists" do
    card = cards(:buy_domain)
    visit_board

    assert_selector "#maybe ##{dom_id(card, :article)}"
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(@in_progress)} .cards__expander-count", text: "1"

    drag_card_to_column card, "##{dom_id(@in_progress)}"

    assert_no_selector "#maybe ##{dom_id(card, :article)}"
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(@in_progress)} .cards__expander-count", text: "2"
    assert_selector "#maybe .cards__expander-count", text: "0"

    # Expand the target column — card is already there with the column's color
    expand_column "##{dom_id(@in_progress)}"
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(@in_progress)} ##{dom_id(card, :article)}"
    assert_equal @in_progress.color.to_s, card_color_var(card)

    wait_until { card.reload.column == @in_progress }
    assert_equal @in_progress, card.reload.column

    # Reload board and verify exact same order — nothing shifted
    order_before_reload = card_ids_in("##{dom_id(@in_progress)}")
    visit_board
    expand_column "##{dom_id(@in_progress)}"
    assert_equal order_before_reload, card_ids_in("##{dom_id(@in_progress)}")
  end

  test "dragging a card between custom columns, to Maybe, to Not Now, and to Done" do
    card = cards(:text) # starts in writebook_in_progress
    visit_board

    # Custom column -> another custom column (empty On Hold)
    expand_column "##{dom_id(@in_progress)}"
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(@in_progress)} ##{dom_id(card, :article)}"

    drag_card_to_column card, "##{dom_id(@on_hold)}"

    # Source column immediately shows drag blank slate since it is now empty
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(@in_progress)} .blank-slate--drag", visible: true
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(@on_hold)} .cards__expander-count", text: "1"
    wait_until { card.reload.column == @on_hold }

    # Custom column -> Maybe?
    expand_column "##{dom_id(@on_hold)}"
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(@on_hold)} ##{dom_id(card, :article)}"
    drag_card_to_column card, "#maybe"

    assert_selector "#maybe ##{dom_id(card, :article)}"
    assert_equal "var(--color-card-default)", card_color_var(card)
    wait_until { card.reload.awaiting_triage? }

    # Maybe? -> Not Now
    drag_card_to_column card, "#not-now"
    assert_no_selector "#maybe ##{dom_id(card, :article)}"
    assert_selector "#not-now .cards__expander-count", text: "1"
    wait_until { card.reload.postponed? }

    # Not Now -> Done
    expand_column "#not-now"
    assert_selector "#not-now ##{dom_id(card, :article)}"
    drag_card_to_column card, "#closed-cards"
    assert_selector "#not-now .blank-slate--drag", visible: true
    assert_selector "#closed-cards .cards__expander-count", text: "2"
    wait_until { card.reload.closed? }

    # Done -> Custom column (reopens and triages)
    expand_column "#closed-cards"
    assert_selector "#closed-cards ##{dom_id(card, :article)}"
    drag_card_to_column card, "##{dom_id(@in_progress)}"
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(@closed_cards_id)} .cards__expander-count", text: "1"
    wait_until { card.reload.triaged? && card.column == @in_progress }

    expand_column "##{dom_id(@in_progress)}"
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(@in_progress)} ##{dom_id(card, :article)}.card--active"
    assert_no_selector "##{dom_id(card, :article)}.card--postponed"
    assert_equal @in_progress.color.to_s, card_color_var(card)
  end

  test "dragging a closed card to Not Now postpones it without duplicate reopen events" do
    card = cards(:shipping) # starts closed
    visit_board

    expand_column "#closed-cards"
    assert_selector "#closed-cards ##{dom_id(card, :article)}"

    before_reopened = card.events.where(action: "card_reopened").count
    drag_card_to_column card, "#not-now"

    assert_selector "#not-now .cards__expander-count", text: "1"
    assert_selector "#closed-cards .cards__expander-count", text: "0"

    wait_until { card.reload.postponed? }
    assert_not card.reload.closed?
    assert_equal before_reopened + 1, card.events.where(action: "card_reopened").count
  end

  test "dropping a card back onto its own column does not reorder or persist" do
    visit_board
    expand_column "##{dom_id(@triage)}"

    initial_order = card_ids_in("##{dom_id(@triage)}")
    assert_equal 2, initial_order.length

    second_card_id = initial_order.last
    second_card = cards(:logo)
    second_card = cards(:layout) if dom_id(second_card, :article) != second_card_id
    original_last_active = second_card.last_active_at

    # Track fetch calls to make sure no request is fired
    page.execute_script(<<~JS)
      window.__dndFetchCount = 0
      const origFetch = window.fetch
      window.__origFetch = origFetch
      window.fetch = function(...args) {
        window.__dndFetchCount++
        return origFetch.apply(this, args)
      }
    JS

    drag_card_to_column second_card, "##{dom_id(@triage)}"

    assert_equal initial_order, card_ids_in("##{dom_id(@triage)}")
    assert_equal 0, page.evaluate_script("window.__dndFetchCount")
    assert_equal original_last_active.to_i, second_card.reload.last_active_at.to_i
  ensure
    page.execute_script("if (window.__origFetch) window.fetch = window.__origFetch")
  end

  test "columns keep their own order with golden cards and nothing shifts on reload" do
    # Make logo golden in Triage; layout is non-golden in Triage
    cards(:logo).gild
    # buy_domain is non-golden in Maybe?
    non_golden = cards(:buy_domain)
    # text is golden in In progress
    golden = cards(:text)
    golden.gild

    visit_board
    expand_column "##{dom_id(@triage)}"
    assert_equal [ dom_id(cards(:logo), :article), dom_id(cards(:layout), :article) ], card_ids_in("##{dom_id(@triage)}")

    # 1. Drag non-golden card into Triage -> must land AFTER golden card (logo) and BEFORE older non-golden (layout)
    drag_card_to_column non_golden, "##{dom_id(@triage)}"
    expected_after_non_golden = [
      dom_id(cards(:logo), :article),
      dom_id(non_golden, :article),
      dom_id(cards(:layout), :article)
    ]
    assert_equal expected_after_non_golden, card_ids_in("##{dom_id(@triage)}")
    wait_until { non_golden.reload.column == @triage }

    visit_board
    expand_column "##{dom_id(@triage)}"
    assert_equal expected_after_non_golden, card_ids_in("##{dom_id(@triage)}")

    # 2. Drag golden card from In progress into Triage -> must land at VERY TOP (before older golden logo)
    expand_column "##{dom_id(@in_progress)}"
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(@in_progress)} ##{dom_id(golden, :article)}"
    drag_card_to_column golden, "##{dom_id(@triage)}"
    wait_until { golden.reload.column == @triage }

    expand_column "##{dom_id(@triage)}"
    expected_after_golden = [
      dom_id(golden, :article),
      dom_id(cards(:logo), :article),
      dom_id(non_golden, :article),
      dom_id(cards(:layout), :article)
    ]
    assert_equal expected_after_golden, card_ids_in("##{dom_id(@triage)}")

    visit_board
    expand_column "##{dom_id(@triage)}"
    assert_equal expected_after_golden, card_ids_in("##{dom_id(@triage)}")

    # 3. Drag non-golden card into Done when Done has a golden card -> Done sorts by recently_closed_first (NOT golden-first)
    cards(:shipping).gild
    visit_board
    expand_column "#closed-cards"
    assert_equal [ dom_id(cards(:shipping), :article) ], card_ids_in("#closed-cards")

    # Drag non-golden buy_domain from Triage -> expand Triage first, drop onto collapsed Done
    expand_column "##{dom_id(@triage)}"
    drag_card_to_column non_golden, "#closed-cards"
    wait_until { non_golden.reload.closed? }

    expand_column "#closed-cards"
    expected_done_order = [
      dom_id(non_golden, :article),
      dom_id(cards(:shipping), :article)
    ]
    assert_equal expected_done_order, card_ids_in("#closed-cards")

    visit_board
    expand_column "#closed-cards"
    assert_equal expected_done_order, card_ids_in("#closed-cards")
  end

  test "visual styles: dragged card dims and hovered column lights up without flickering" do
    card = cards(:buy_domain)
    visit_board
    expand_column "##{dom_id(@triage)}"

    card_selector = "##{dom_id(card, :article)}"
    triage_selector = "##{dom_id(@triage)}"

    # Start dragging card in Maybe?
    page.execute_script(<<~JS, card_selector)
      const card = document.querySelector(arguments[0])
      const dt = new DataTransfer()
      window.__dndDT = dt
      card.dispatchEvent(new DragEvent("dragstart", { bubbles: true, cancelable: true, dataTransfer: dt }))
    JS

    # Card dims with drag-and-drop__dragged-item
    assert_selector "#{card_selector}.drag-and-drop__dragged-item"

    # Dragging over source column (#maybe) does NOT light up #maybe
    page.execute_script(<<~JS)
      const maybe = document.querySelector("#maybe")
      maybe.dispatchEvent(new DragEvent("dragenter", { bubbles: true, cancelable: true, dataTransfer: window.__dndDT }))
      maybe.dispatchEvent(new DragEvent("dragover", { bubbles: true, cancelable: true, dataTransfer: window.__dndDT }))
    JS
    assert_no_selector "#maybe.drag-and-drop__hover-container"

    # Dragging over target column lights it up
    page.execute_script(<<~JS, triage_selector)
      const triage = document.querySelector(arguments[0])
      triage.dispatchEvent(new DragEvent("dragenter", { bubbles: true, cancelable: true, dataTransfer: window.__dndDT }))
      triage.dispatchEvent(new DragEvent("dragover", { bubbles: true, cancelable: true, dataTransfer: window.__dndDT }))
    JS
    assert_selector "#{triage_selector}.drag-and-drop__hover-container"

    # Moving across child elements inside Triage (dragleave with relatedTarget inside triage) keeps highlight on
    page.execute_script(<<~JS, triage_selector)
      const triage = document.querySelector(arguments[0])
      const child = triage.querySelector(".cards__list")
      triage.dispatchEvent(new DragEvent("dragleave", { bubbles: true, cancelable: true, relatedTarget: child, dataTransfer: window.__dndDT }))
    JS
    assert_selector "#{triage_selector}.drag-and-drop__hover-container"

    # Moving outside Triage removes highlight
    page.execute_script(<<~JS, triage_selector)
      const triage = document.querySelector(arguments[0])
      triage.dispatchEvent(new DragEvent("dragleave", { bubbles: true, cancelable: true, relatedTarget: document.body, dataTransfer: window.__dndDT }))
    JS
    assert_no_selector "#{triage_selector}.drag-and-drop__hover-container"

    # Canceling drag (dragend) clears dragged item dim class
    page.execute_script(<<~JS, card_selector)
      const card = document.querySelector(arguments[0])
      card.dispatchEvent(new DragEvent("dragend", { bubbles: true, dataTransfer: window.__dndDT }))
    JS
    assert_no_selector "#{card_selector}.drag-and-drop__dragged-item"
  end

  test "drop is instant before save completes and nothing shifts afterwards" do
    card = cards(:buy_domain)
    visit_board
    expand_column "##{dom_id(@triage)}"

    # Intercept fetch so we can pause the save and inspect the DOM BEFORE the server responds
    page.execute_script(<<~JS)
      window.__pendingResolvers = []
      const origFetch = window.fetch
      window.__origFetch = origFetch
      window.fetch = function(url, options) {
        if (options && (options.method === "POST" || options.method === "DELETE")) {
          return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
            window.__pendingResolvers.push(() => {
              origFetch.call(window, url, options).then(resolve, reject)
            })
          })
        }
        return origFetch.apply(this, arguments)
      }
    JS

    drag_card_to_column card, "##{dom_id(@triage)}"

    # Save has NOT been sent yet, but DOM is ALREADY updated!
    assert_equal 1, page.evaluate_script("window.__pendingResolvers.length")
    assert_no_selector "#maybe ##{dom_id(card, :article)}"
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(@triage)} ##{dom_id(card, :article)}"
    assert_equal @triage.color.to_s, card_color_var(card)
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(@triage)} .cards__expander-count", text: "3"
    assert_selector "#maybe .cards__expander-count", text: "0"
    assert_nil card.reload.column # still unsaved in DB

    dom_order_before_save = card_ids_in("##{dom_id(@triage)}")

    # Release the save
    page.execute_script("window.__pendingResolvers.shift()()")
    wait_until { card.reload.column == @triage }

    # Nothing shifted after the save completed
    assert_equal dom_order_before_save, card_ids_in("##{dom_id(@triage)}")
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(@triage)} .cards__expander-count", text: "3"
  ensure
    page.execute_script("if (window.__origFetch) window.fetch = window.__origFetch")
  end

  test "reverts the optimistic move when the server save fails" do
    card = cards(:buy_domain)
    visit_board
    expand_column "##{dom_id(@triage)}"

    page.execute_script(<<~JS)
      const origFetch = window.fetch
      window.__origFetch = origFetch
      window.fetch = function(url, options) {
        if (options && options.method === "POST") {
          return Promise.resolve(new Response(null, { status: 500 }))
        }
        return origFetch.apply(this, arguments)
      }
    JS

    drag_card_to_column card, "##{dom_id(@triage)}"

    # Rollback restores card to Maybe? with original color and counts
    assert_selector "#maybe ##{dom_id(card, :article)}"
    assert_no_selector "##{dom_id(@triage)} ##{dom_id(card, :article)}"
    assert_equal "var(--color-card-default)", card_color_var(card)
    assert_selector "#maybe .cards__expander-count", text: "1"
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(@triage)} .cards__expander-count", text: "2"
  ensure
    page.execute_script("if (window.__origFetch) window.fetch = window.__origFetch")
  end

  test "rapid consecutive drags of the same card execute in order" do
    card = cards(:buy_domain)
    visit_board
    expand_column "##{dom_id(@triage)}"

    drag_card_to_column card, "##{dom_id(@triage)}"
    drag_card_to_column card, "#closed-cards"

    assert_no_selector "#maybe ##{dom_id(card, :article)}"
    assert_no_selector "##{dom_id(@triage)} ##{dom_id(card, :article)}"
    assert_selector "#closed-cards .cards__expander-count", text: "2"

    wait_until { card.reload.closed? }
    assert card.reload.closed?
  end

  test "clicking a draggable card still opens the card" do
    card = cards(:buy_domain)
    visit_board

    assert_equal true, page.evaluate_script("document.querySelector('##{dom_id(card, :article)}').draggable")
    find("##{dom_id(card, :article)} a.card__link").click

    assert_selector "h1", text: card.title
  end

  test "draggable attribute is preserved after a Turbo morph refresh" do
    card = cards(:buy_domain)
    visit_board
    assert_equal true, page.evaluate_script("document.querySelector('##{dom_id(card, :article)}').draggable")

    # Simulate a Turbo morph refresh on the board
    page.execute_script("Turbo.session.refresh(document.baseURI)")
    sleep 0.3

    assert_equal true, page.evaluate_script("document.querySelector('##{dom_id(card, :article)}').draggable")
  end

  test "cards are not draggable on small viewports or public boards" do
    card = cards(:buy_domain)

    # Small viewport (< 640px)
    page.current_window.resize_to(500, 800)
    visit_board
    assert_equal false, page.evaluate_script("document.querySelector('##{dom_id(card, :article)}').draggable")
    page.current_window.resize_to(1200, 1000)

    # Public board
    @board.publish
    visit public_board_url(@board.publication.key)
    assert_selector "#maybe ##{dom_id(card, :article)}"
    assert_no_selector '[data-controller~="drag-and-drop"]'
    assert_equal false, page.evaluate_script("document.querySelector('##{dom_id(card, :article)}').draggable")
  end

  test "real browser drag_to moves card to another column" do
    card = cards(:buy_domain)
    visit_board
    expand_column "##{dom_id(@triage)}"

    card_el = find("##{dom_id(card, :article)}")
    triage_el = find("##{dom_id(@triage)}")
    card_el.drag_to(triage_el)

    assert_selector "##{dom_id(@triage)} ##{dom_id(card, :article)}"
    wait_until { card.reload.column == @triage }
    assert_equal @triage, card.reload.column
  end

  private
    def visit_board
      visit board_url(@board)
      # Wait for column frames to finish loading
      assert_selector "##{dom_id(@triage)}_cards .cards__list", visible: :all
      assert_selector "#closed_column .cards__list", visible: :all
      assert_selector "#not_now_column .cards__list", visible: :all
    end

    def expand_column(selector)
      if has_selector?("#{selector}.is-collapsed", wait: 0.2)
        find("#{selector} .cards__expander").click
      end
      assert_selector "#{selector}.is-expanded"
    end

    def drag_card_to_column(card, column_selector)
      card_selector = "##{dom_id(card, :article)}"
      page.execute_script(<<~JS, card_selector, column_selector)
        const card = document.querySelector(arguments[0])
        const target = document.querySelector(arguments[1])
        const dt = new DataTransfer()
        card.dispatchEvent(new DragEvent("dragstart", { bubbles: true, cancelable: true, dataTransfer: dt }))
        target.dispatchEvent(new DragEvent("dragenter", { bubbles: true, cancelable: true, dataTransfer: dt }))
        target.dispatchEvent(new DragEvent("dragover", { bubbles: true, cancelable: true, dataTransfer: dt }))
        target.dispatchEvent(new DragEvent("drop", { bubbles: true, cancelable: true, dataTransfer: dt }))

steps.reasoning_content:

The order of arguments to `dom_id` is crucial. The prefix (the second argument, in this case `:cards`) comes *before* the object's ID in the generated HTML! So `dom_id(column, :cards)` produces `cards_column_<id>`, not the other way around. 

The test helper was the culprit! I can see it now: `column_frame_tag dom_id(column, :cards)` correctly generates `id="cards_column_03axmcferfmbnv4qg816nw6bg"`, yet our test helper was using `##{dom_id(@triage)}_cards` instead of `##{dom_id(@triage, :cards)}`. That's where I was going wrong!

As a side note, it's worth remembering that running `bin/rails test:system test/system/board_drag_and_drop_test.rb` runs ALL system tests, not just the one I wanted. I should use `bin/rails test test/system/board_drag_and_drop_test.rb` to run the specific test file.

steps.reasoning_content:
Okay, here's my take on those changes:

**Refactoring `Postponable` and `Closeable` and Adding Tests**

Alright, time to clean up some of our card models and add some robust testing. I'm thinking we should make some crucial updates to the `Postponable` and `Closeable` concerns within our application. Specifically, in `app/models/card/postponable.rb` and `app/models/card/closeable.rb`, I want to make sure the `postpone` method is truly *idempotent*. That is, calling it multiple times shouldn't cause unintended side effects or errors. It should be safe to call repeatedly. Additionally, I want to ensure that `resume`, `close`, and `reopen` correctly handle resetting their associated `has_one` associations when a card has been destroyed. We need to make these actions clean and predictable.

To ensure everything works as expected and stays that way, I'll be adding comprehensive model tests. I'm planning a new test file, `test/models/card/postponable_test.rb`. In it, I want to specifically test the scenarios of postponing a card that's *already* closed and postponing a card that's *already* postponed. This will help prevent regressions and ensure the idempotency of the postpone function. We need to make sure we're handling all edge cases.

cat <<'EOF' > app/models/card/postponable.rb
module Card::Postponable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    has_one :not_now, dependent: :destroy, class_name: "Card::NotNow"

    scope :postponed, -> { open.published.joins(:not_now) }
    scope :active, -> { open.published.where.missing(:not_now) }
  end

  def postponed?
    open? && published? && not_now.present?
  end

  def postponed_at
    not_now&.created_at
  end

  def postponed_by
    not_now&.user
  end

  def active?
    open? && published? && !postponed?
  end

  def auto_postpone(**args)
    postpone(**args, event_name: :auto_postponed)
  end

  def postpone(user: Current.user, event_name: :postponed)
    unless postponed?
      transaction do
        send_back_to_triage(skip_event: true)
        reopen
        activity_spike&.destroy
        create_not_now!(user: user)
        track_event event_name, creator: user
      end
    end
  end

  def resume
    transaction do
      reopen
      activity_spike&.destroy
      not_now&.destroy
      association(:not_now).reset
    end
  end
end
EOF

cat <<'EOF' > app/models/card/closeable.rb
module Card::Closeable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    has_one :closure, dependent: :destroy

    scope :closed, -> { joins(:closure) }
    scope :open, -> { where.missing(:closure) }

    scope :recently_closed_first, -> { closed.order(closures: { created_at: :desc }) }
    scope :closed_at_window, ->(window) { closed.where(closures: { created_at: window }) }
    scope :closed_by, ->(users) { closed.where(closures: { user_id: Array(users) }) }
  end

  def closed?
    closure.present?
  end

  def open?
    !closed?
  end

  def closed_by
    closure&.user
  end

  def closed_at
    closure&.created_at
  end

  def close(user: Current.user)
    unless closed?
      transaction do
        not_now&.destroy
        association(:not_now).reset
        create_closure! user: user
        track_event :closed, creator: user
      end
    end
  end

  def reopen(user: Current.user)
    if closed?
      transaction do
        closure&.destroy
        association(:closure).reset
        track_event :reopened, creator: user
      end
    end
  end
end
EOF

**Expanding System Tests for Robust Drag-and-Drop Functionality**

Okay, time to really put our system tests in `test/system/board_drag_and_drop_test.rb` through their paces. We've got a comprehensive list of adversarial scenarios we need to cover to ensure our drag-and-drop implementation is truly robust.

First, the cross-browser refresh scenario is critical. We need to verify that a drag-and-drop action in one browser window triggers a correct update in another window (`within_window(open_new_window)`) and *crucially*, that the initiating window doesn't unnecessarily refresh itself (we'll leverage the `X-Turbo-Request-Id` to verify this deduplication).

Next, we'll test dragging into a brand-new column that's created on the fly. We'll add a new column, let's call it "QA", and immediately drag a card into it to ensure that interaction is flawless.

We also have to confirm that our CSS styles from `drag_and_drop.css` and `card-columns.css` are being correctly applied. That `opacity: 0.6` on the dragged item and the dashed outline on the hover container are essential for a good user experience.

Then, we need to handle some edge cases. If we drag a non-golden card into a column with *only* golden cards, the system should correctly position it *after* the last golden card. Also, dragging a card into "Not Now" when "Not Now" already contains a golden card has to place the new card at the very top, to match the `.postponed.latest` behavior, without any golden-first prioritization here.

We also need to test dragging cards out of an entropy-bubbled or postponed state, to ensure the visual state transitions cleanly. We want to verify that the `.bubble` and `.card__closed` classes are properly removed so the color doesn't get stuck gray.

Finally, we'll round things out with some unit tests in `test/models/card/postponable_test.rb` to cover the cases of postponing a closed card and postponing a card that's already postponed.

require "test_helper"

class Card::PostponableTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  setup do
    Current.session = sessions(:david)
  end

  test "check the postponed status of a card" do
    card = cards(:logo)

    assert_not card.postponed?
    assert card.active?

    card.postpone
    assert card.postponed?
    assert_not card.active?
  end

  test "postpone and resume a card" do
    card = cards(:text)

    assert_changes -> { card.reload.postponed? }, to: true do
      assert_difference -> { card.events.count }, +1 do
        card.postpone
      end
    end

    assert_equal users(:david), card.not_now.user
    assert card.events.last.action.card_postponed?

    assert_changes -> { card.reload.postponed? }, to: false do
      card.resume
    end
  end

  test "postpone is idempotent when already postponed" do
    card = cards(:text)
    card.postpone

    assert_no_difference -> { card.events.count } do
      card.postpone
    end

    assert card.reload.postponed?
  end

  test "postpone a closed card reopens it once and postpones it" do
    card = cards(:shipping)
    assert card.closed?

    assert_difference -> { card.events.where(action: "card_reopened").count }, +1 do
      assert_difference -> { card.events.where(action: "card_postponed").count }, +1 do
        card.postpone
      end
    end

    assert card.reload.postponed?
    assert_not card.closed?
  end

  test "auto_postpone a card" do
    card = cards(:text)

    assert_changes -> { card.reload.postponed? }, to: true do
      assert_difference -> { card.events.count }, +1 do
        card.auto_postpone
      end
    end

    assert card.events.last.action.card_auto_postponed?
  end

  test "scopes" do
    logo = cards(:logo)
    text = cards(:text)

    logo.postpone

    assert_includes Card.postponed, logo
    assert_not_includes Card.postponed, text

    assert_includes Card.active, text
    assert_not_includes Card.active, logo
  end
end
EOF

require "application_system_test_case"

class BoardDragAndDropTest < ApplicationSystemTestCase
  include ActionView::RecordIdentifier

  setup do
    sign_in_as(users(:david))
    @board = boards(:writebook)
    @triage = columns(:writebook_triage)
    @in_progress = columns(:writebook_in_progress)
    @on_hold = columns(:writebook_on_hold)
  end

  test "dragging a card from Maybe to a collapsed column updates immediately and persists" do
    card = cards(:buy_domain)
    visit_board

    assert_selector "#maybe ##{dom_id(card, :article)}"
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(@in_progress)} .cards__expander-count", text: "1"

    drag_card_to_column card, "##{dom_id(@in_progress)}"

    assert_no_selector "#maybe ##{dom_id(card, :article)}"
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(@in_progress)} .cards__expander-count", text: "2"
    assert_selector "#maybe .cards__expander-count", text: "0", visible: :all

    # Expand the target column — card is already there with the column's color
    expand_column "##{dom_id(@in_progress)}"
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(@in_progress)} ##{dom_id(card, :article)}"
    assert_equal @in_progress.color.to_s, card_color_var(card)

    wait_until { card.reload.column == @in_progress }
    assert_equal @in_progress, card.reload.column

    # Reload board and verify exact same order — nothing shifted
    order_before_reload = card_ids_in("##{dom_id(@in_progress)}")
    visit_board
    expand_column "##{dom_id(@in_progress)}"
    assert_equal order_before_reload, card_ids_in("##{dom_id(@in_progress)}")
  end

  test "dragging a card between custom columns, to Maybe, to Not Now, and to Done" do
    card = cards(:text) # starts in writebook_in_progress
    visit_board

    # Custom column -> another custom column (empty On Hold)
    expand_column "##{dom_id(@in_progress)}"
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(@in_progress)} ##{dom_id(card, :article)}"

    drag_card_to_column card, "##{dom_id(@on_hold)}"

    # Source column immediately shows drag blank slate since it is now empty
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(@in_progress)} .blank-slate--drag", visible: true
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(@on_hold)} .cards__expander-count", text: "1"
    wait_until { card.reload.column == @on_hold }

    # Custom column -> Maybe?
    expand_column "##{dom_id(@on_hold)}"
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(@on_hold)} ##{dom_id(card, :article)}"
    drag_card_to_column card, "#maybe"

    assert_selector "#maybe ##{dom_id(card, :article)}"
    assert_equal "var(--color-card-default)", card_color_var(card)
    wait_until { card.reload.awaiting_triage? }

    # Maybe? -> Not Now
    drag_card_to_column card, "#not-now"
    assert_no_selector "#maybe ##{dom_id(card, :article)}"
    assert_selector "#not-now .cards__expander-count", text: "1"
    wait_until { card.reload.postponed? }

    # Not Now -> Done
    expand_column "#not-now"
    assert_selector "#not-now ##{dom_id(card, :article)}"
    drag_card_to_column card, "#closed-cards"
    assert_selector "#not-now .blank-slate--drag", visible: true
    assert_selector "#closed-cards .cards__expander-count", text: "2"
    wait_until { card.reload.closed? }

    # Done -> Custom column (reopens and triages)
    expand_column "#closed-cards"
    assert_selector "#closed-cards ##{dom_id(card, :article)}"
    drag_card_to_column card, "##{dom_id(@in_progress)}"
    assert_selector "#closed-cards .cards__expander-count", text: "1", visible: :all
    wait_until { card.reload.triaged? && card.column == @in_progress }

    expand_column "##{dom_id(@in_progress)}"
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(@in_progress)} ##{dom_id(card, :article)}.card--active"
    assert_no_selector "##{dom_id(card, :article)}.card--postponed"
    assert_no_selector "##{dom_id(card, :article)} .card__closed", visible: :all
    assert_equal @in_progress.color.to_s, card_color_var(card)
  end

  test "dragging a closed card to Not Now postpones it without duplicate reopen events" do
    card = cards(:shipping) # starts closed
    visit_board

    expand_column "#closed-cards"
    assert_selector "#closed-cards ##{dom_id(card, :article)}"

    before_reopened = card.events.where(action: "card_reopened").count

    assert_selector "#not-now .cards__expander-count", text: "1"
    assert_selector "#closed-cards .cards__expander-count", text: "0", visible: :all

    wait_until { card.reload.postponed? }
    assert_not card.reload.closed?
    assert_equal before_reopened + 1, card.events.where(action: "card_reopened").count

  test "dropping a card back onto its own column does not reorder or persist" do

    drag_card_to_column non_golden, "#closed-cards"
    wait_until { non_golden.reload.closed? }

    visit_board
    expand_column "#closed-cards"
    assert_equal expected_done_order, card_ids_in("#closed-cards")

    # 5. Non-golden into Not Now with a golden card -> Not Now sorts latest (top, NOT golden-first)
    golden.postpone
    visit_board
    expand_column "#closed-cards"
    drag_card_to_column non_golden, "#not-now"
    wait_until { non_golden.reload.postponed? }

    expand_column "#not-now"
    expected_not_now_order = [
      dom_id(non_golden, :article),
      dom_id(golden, :article)
    ]
    assert_equal expected_not_now_order, card_ids_in("#not-now")

    visit_board
    expand_column "#not-now"
    assert_equal expected_not_now_order, card_ids_in("#not-now")
  end

  test "visual styles: dragged card dims and hovered column lights up without flickering" do
    card = cards(:buy_domain)
    visit_board
    expand_column "##{dom_id(@triage)}"

    card_selector = "##{dom_id(card, :article)}"
    triage_selector = "##{dom_id(@triage)}"

    page.execute_script(<<~JS, card_selector)
      const card = document.querySelector(arguments[0])
      const dt = new DataTransfer()
      window.__dndDT = dt
      card.dispatchEvent(new DragEvent("dragstart", { bubbles: true, cancelable: true, dataTransfer: dt }))
    JS

    # Card dims with drag-and-drop__dragged-item and computed opacity is 0.6
    assert_selector "#{card_selector}.drag-and-drop__dragged-item"
    assert_equal "0.6", page.evaluate_script("getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('#{card_selector}')).opacity")
    assert_equal "dashed", page.evaluate_script("getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('#{card_selector}')).outlineStyle")

    # Dragging over source column (#maybe) does NOT light up #maybe
    page.execute_script(<<~JS)
      const maybe = document.querySelector("#maybe")
      maybe.dispatchEvent(new DragEvent("dragenter", { bubbles: true, cancelable: true, dataTransfer: window.__dndDT }))
      maybe.dispatchEvent(new DragEvent("dragover", { bubbles: true, cancelable: true, dataTransfer: window.__dndDT }))
    JS
    assert_no_selector "#maybe.drag-and-drop__hover-container"

    # Dragging over target column lights it up with dashed outline
    page.execute_script(<<~JS, triage_selector)
      const triage = document.querySelector(arguments[0])
      triage.dispatchEvent(new DragEvent("dragenter", { bubbles: true, cancelable: true, dataTransfer: window.__dndDT }))
      triage.dispatchEvent(new DragEvent("dragover", { bubbles: true, cancelable: true, dataTransfer: window.__dndDT }))
    JS
    assert_selector "#{triage_selector}.drag-and-drop__hover-container"
    assert_equal "dashed", page.evaluate_script("getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('#{triage_selector} .cards__transition-container')).outlineStyle")

    # Moving across child elements inside Triage keeps highlight on
    page.execute_script(<<~JS, triage_selector)
      const triage = document.querySelector(arguments[0])
      const child = triage.querySelector(".cards__list")
      triage.dispatchEvent(new DragEvent("dragleave", { bubbles: true, cancelable: true, relatedTarget: child, dataTransfer: window.__dndDT }))
    JS
    assert_selector "#{triage_selector}.drag-and-drop__hover-container"

    # Moving outside Triage removes highlight
    page.execute_script(<<~JS, triage_selector)
      const triage = document.querySelector(arguments[0])
      triage.dispatchEvent(new DragEvent("dragleave", { bubbles: true, cancelable: true, relatedTarget: document.body, dataTransfer: window.__dndDT }))
    JS
    assert_no_selector "#{triage_selector}.drag-and-drop__hover-container"

    # Canceling drag (dragend) clears dragged item dim class
    page.execute_script(<<~JS, card_selector)
      const card = document.querySelector(arguments[0])
      card.dispatchEvent(new DragEvent("dragend", { bubbles: true, dataTransfer: window.__dndDT }))
    JS
    assert_no_selector "#{card_selector}.drag-and-drop__dragged-item"
  end

  test "drop is instant before save completes and nothing shifts afterwards" do
    card = cards(:buy_domain)
    visit_board
    expand_column "##{dom_id(@triage)}"

    page.execute_script(<<~JS)
      window.__pendingResolvers = []
      window.__sentTurboRequestIds = []
      const origFetch = window.fetch
      window.__origFetch = origFetch
      window.fetch = function(url, options) {
        if (options && (options.method === "POST" || options.method === "DELETE")) {
          const reqId = options.headers instanceof Headers
            ? options.headers.get("X-Turbo-Request-Id")
            : options.headers?.["X-Turbo-Request-Id"]
          window.__sentTurboRequestIds.push(reqId)
          return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
            window.__pendingResolvers.push(() => {
              origFetch.call(window, url, options).then(resolve, reject)
            })
          })
        }
        return origFetch.apply(this, arguments)
      }
    JS

    drag_card_to_column card, "##{dom_id(@triage)}"

    # Save has NOT been sent yet, but DOM is ALREADY updated!
    assert_equal 1, page.evaluate_script("window.__pendingResolvers.length")
    assert_not_nil page.evaluate_script("window.__sentTurboRequestIds[0]")
    assert_no_selector "#maybe ##{dom_id(card, :article)}"
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(@triage)} ##{dom_id(card, :article)}"
    assert_equal @triage.color.to_s, card_color_var(card)
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(@triage)} .cards__expander-count", text: "3", visible: :all
    assert_selector "#maybe .cards__expander-count", text: "0", visible: :all
    assert_nil card.reload.column

    dom_order_before_save = card_ids_in("##{dom_id(@triage)}")

    # Release the save
    page.execute_script("window.__pendingResolvers.shift()()")
    wait_until { card.reload.column == @triage }

    # Nothing shifted after the save completed
    assert_equal dom_order_before_save, card_ids_in("##{dom_id(@triage)}")
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(@triage)} .cards__expander-count", text: "3", visible: :all
  ensure
    page.execute_script("if (window.__origFetch) window.fetch = window.__origFetch")
  end

  test "reverts the optimistic move when the server save fails" do
    card = cards(:buy_domain)
    visit_board
    expand_column "##{dom_id(@triage)}"

    page.execute_script(<<~JS)
      const origFetch = window.fetch
      window.__origFetch = origFetch
      window.fetch = function(url, options) {
        if (options && options.method === "POST") {
          return Promise.resolve(new Response(null, { status: 500 }))
        }
        return origFetch.apply(this, arguments)
      }
    JS

    drag_card_to_column card, "##{dom_id(@triage)}"

    assert_selector "#maybe ##{dom_id(card, :article)}"
    assert_no_selector "##{dom_id(@triage)} ##{dom_id(card, :article)}"
    assert_equal "var(--color-card-default)", card_color_var(card)
    assert_selector "#maybe .cards__expander-count", text: "1", visible: :all
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(@triage)} .cards__expander-count", text: "2", visible: :all
  ensure
    page.execute_script("if (window.__origFetch) window.fetch = window.__origFetch")
  end

  test "rapid consecutive drags of the same card execute in order" do
    card = cards(:buy_domain)
    visit_board
    expand_column "##{dom_id(@triage)}"

    drag_card_to_column card, "##{dom_id(@triage)}"
    drag_card_to_column card, "#closed-cards"

    assert_no_selector "#maybe ##{dom_id(card, :article)}"
    assert_no_selector "##{dom_id(@triage)} ##{dom_id(card, :article)}"
    assert_selector "#closed-cards .cards__expander-count", text: "2"

    wait_until { card.reload.closed? }
    assert card.reload.closed?
  end

  test "dragging a card into a newly created column works immediately" do
    card = cards(:buy_domain)
    visit_board

    find(".cards__new-column > button").click
    within ".cards__new-column dialog[open]" do
      fill_in "Name this column…", with: "QA"
      click_on "Add column"
    end

    assert_selector ".cards[data-column-name='QA']"
    qa_column = @board.columns.find_by!(name: "QA")
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(qa_column, :cards)} .cards__list", visible: :all

    drag_card_to_column card, "##{dom_id(qa_column)}"

    assert_no_selector "#maybe ##{dom_id(card, :article)}"
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(qa_column)} .cards__expander-count", text: "1"
    wait_until { card.reload.column == qa_column }
  end

  test "clicking a draggable card still opens the card" do
    card = cards(:buy_domain)
    visit_board

    assert_equal true, page.evaluate_script("document.querySelector('##{dom_id(card, :article)}').draggable")
    find("##{dom_id(card, :article)} a.card__link").click

    assert_selector "h1", text: card.title
  end

  test "draggable attribute is preserved after a Turbo morph refresh and other windows see broadcast updates" do
    card = cards(:buy_domain)
    visit_board
    wait_for_cable_subscriptions

    assert_equal true, page.evaluate_script("document.querySelector('##{dom_id(card, :article)}').draggable")

    # Open a second window viewing the same board
    other_window = open_new_window
    within_window(other_window) do
      visit_board
      wait_for_cable_subscriptions
      assert_selector "#maybe ##{dom_id(card, :article)}"
    end

    # Track whether the initiating window triggers a Turbo refresh visit when its own broadcast arrives
    page.execute_script(<<~JS)
      window.__selfRefreshVisits = 0
      document.addEventListener("turbo:before-visit", () => window.__selfRefreshVisits++)
    JS

    drag_card_to_column card, "##{dom_id(@in_progress)}"
    wait_until { card.reload.column == @in_progress }
    perform_enqueued_jobs only: Turbo::Streams::BroadcastStreamJob

    # Other window refreshes via ActionCable and shows the card in In progress
    within_window(other_window) do
      assert_no_selector "#maybe ##{dom_id(card, :article)}", wait: 5
      assert_selector "##{dom_id(@in_progress)} .cards__expander-count", text: "2", wait: 5
    end

    # Initiating window ignored its own broadcast (no self-refresh visit!)
    assert_equal 0, page.evaluate_script("window.__selfRefreshVisits")

    # Even when an external Turbo morph refresh DOES happen, draggable stays true
    page.execute_script("Turbo.session.refresh(document.baseURI)")
    sleep 0.3
    assert_equal true, page.evaluate_script("document.querySelector('##{dom_id(card, :article)}').draggable")
  end

  test "cards are not draggable on small viewports or public boards" do
    card = cards(:buy_domain)

    page.current_window.resize_to(500, 800)
    visit_board
    assert_equal false, page.evaluate_script("document.querySelector('##{dom_id(card, :article)}').draggable")
    page.current_window.resize_to(1200, 1000)

    @board.publish
    visit public_board_url(@board.publication.key)
    assert_selector "#maybe ##{dom_id(card, :article)}"
    assert_no_selector '[data-controller~="drag-and-drop"]'
    assert_equal false, page.evaluate_script("document.querySelector('##{dom_id(card, :article)}').draggable")
  end

  test "real browser drag_to moves card to another column" do
    card = cards(:buy_domain)
    visit_board
    expand_column "##{dom_id(@triage)}"

    card_el = find("##{dom_id(card, :article)}")
    triage_el = find("##{dom_id(@triage)}")
    card_el.drag_to(triage_el)

    assert_selector "##{dom_id(@triage)} ##{dom_id(card, :article)}"
    wait_until { card.reload.column == @triage }
    assert_equal @triage, card.reload.column
  end

  private
    def visit_board
      visit board_url(@board)
      assert_selector "##{dom_id(@triage, :cards)} .cards__list", visible: :all
      assert_selector "#closed_column .cards__list", visible: :all
      assert_selector "#not_now_column .cards__list", visible: :all
    end

    def wait_for_cable_subscriptions
      assert_selector "turbo-cable-stream-source[connected]", visible: :all
      assert_no_selector "turbo-cable-stream-source:not([connected])", visible: :all
    end

    def expand_column(selector)
      if has_selector?("#{selector}.is-collapsed", wait: 0.2)
        find("#{selector} .cards__expander").click
      end
      assert_selector "#{selector}.is-expanded"
    end

    def drag_card_to_column(card, column_selector)
      card_selector = "##{dom_id(card, :article)}"
      page.execute_script(<<~JS, card_selector, column_selector)
        const card = document.querySelector(arguments[0])
        const target = document.querySelector(arguments[1])
        const dt = new DataTransfer()
        card.dispatchEvent(new DragEvent("dragstart", { bubbles: true, cancelable: true, dataTransfer: dt }))
        target.dispatchEvent(new DragEvent("dragenter", { bubbles: true, cancelable: true, dataTransfer: dt }))
        target.dispatchEvent(new DragEvent("dragover", { bubbles: true, cancelable: true, dataTransfer: dt }))
        target.dispatchEvent(new DragEvent("drop", { bubbles: true, cancelable: true, dataTransfer: dt }))
        card.dispatchEvent(new DragEvent("dragend", { bubbles: true, cancelable: true, dataTransfer: dt }))
      JS
    end

    def card_ids_in(column_selector)
      page.evaluate_script(<<~JS, column_selector)
        Array.from(document.querySelectorAll(arguments[0] + ' .cards__list [data-drag-and-drop-target~="item"]')).map(el => el.id)
      JS
    end

    def card_color_var(card)
      page.evaluate_script(<<~JS, "##{dom_id(card, :article)}")
        document.querySelector(arguments[0]).style.getPropertyValue("--card-color").trim()
      JS
    end

    def wait_until(timeout: 5)
      deadline = Time.now + timeout
      loop do
        return if yield
        raise "Timed out waiting for condition" if Time.now > deadline
        sleep 0.05
      end
    end
end
EOF
